Interest to a bank is simply an expense like any other. The fact they make a profit on it is no different than any other supplier making a profit on what they supply to you. In the case of the bank, they are providing you capital. In the absence of the debt, the business would need to deploy its own capital thus potentially lowering its return. In much the same way you could make everything in house rather than buy from suppliers. Whether you decide to make or buy will depend on the overall effect on total return.

Not every business benefits from debt, but it is definitely a way to increase your profit in the right circumstances. There are other places for debt, too, depending on the business, such as short term revolving credit lines to cover the differences between expense and income cycles, or for development costs secured by a government contract which allows for emergency cash on hand when it would otherwise all be sunk into work in process to an uncomfortable extent.
